source_snapshot.procedure: Enable EDKII injection controls, deploy ITP, boot Windows, log/halt, inspect mc.dimminfo(), inject rank-0 UCE through a socket/channel/dimm/sub_channel tuple, resume, collect photos/results and inspect logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: OS dmesg matches; BMC identifies the DIMM slot with uncorrectable error; front-panel light asserts if present; optional UEFI SEL identifies the slot.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; FAE/operator performs UCE injection and agent tails uncorrected/MCE plus BMC SEL evidence.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; adds controller/DIMM attribution, bounded per-controller injection, crash/recovery, front-panel/UEFI evidence, backup and BIOS restoration.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into Windows. 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on client 5. Using folling command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>mc.dimminfo() >>>ei.injectMemError(socket, channel, dimm, sub_channel,rank=0, errType="uce") >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error if there is one
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Memory controller 1~N (Intel uncorrectable ECC on Memory controller 1~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'uncorrected|UE_|machine.check|MCE_'; echo __uncorrectable_ECC_on_Memory_controller_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: A memory-controller label is a higher-level coverage unit than the injector's DIMM tuple. Multiple channels, sub-channels and ranks may share a controller, so a rank-0 event proves only the approved mapping, not automatically the whole controller or all controllers. Because the source explicitly boots Windows, a Windows RAS/WHEA oracle must replace assumed dmesg. These are resolvable engineering prerequisites, supporting REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION rather than BLOCKED. test_case.test_name: Memory controller 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject one uncorrectable ECC event through every in-scope memory controller, verify the event is attributed to the correct physical DIMM/controller across OS, BMC and recovered UEFI, confirm the front-panel response, and recover the isolated SUT without persistent corruption.
required_package: Supported Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash and UCE consumption/target semantics
Per-controller coverage matrix including whether rank 0 is sufficient
Authoritative Windows/BMC/recovered-UEFI UCE fields and indicator applicability
Crash timeout, console/backup/recovery and post-recovery memory/data-integrity checks
test_case.test_command: An FAE/operator maps memory controllers to socket/channel/DIMM/sub-channel/rank tuples, enables the approved BIOS controls, performs one UCE injection per authorized controller, monitors any crash on an independent console, gathers full pre-crash and recovered evidence plus indicator state, follows the vendor recovery path and restores settings. Controller and rank coverage are approved before execution.
test_case.expected_result: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error if there is one

BMC error log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log should record which slot has DIMM uncorrectable error if there is one`; it becomes enforceable only after resolving: Resolve Reliability row 14 Wistron-System RAS-00734-V003: approve the memory-controller 1~N to socket/channel/DIMM/sub-channel/rank/physical-slot map, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `errType="uce"` semantics; define whether rank=0 tuples cover each controller, bounded count and expected crash; reconcile Windows with dmesg; specify mandatory BMC/UEFI/front-panel evidence, backup, recovery, integrity checks and BIOS restoration.
safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, console, configuration/data backup and FAE approval
Preserve existing evidence instead of clearing logs
Validate each destructive tuple against the controller and physical slot
One injection only per approved target; stop on wrong attribution, uncontrolled MCE, crash beyond plan or data-integrity concern
No automatic retry; restore settings and prove boot/memory health before another target
expected_evidence: Package hash, full `mc.dimminfo()` and controller-to-tuple/rank coverage matrix
Per-controller injection transcript and synchronized crash/recovery timeline
Authoritative Windows UCE/MCE, BMC SEL and recovered UEFI SEL naming the same controller/slot
Front-panel evidence, BIOS restoration, memory/data-integrity and health checks, engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The user/FAE and package gates make a controlled future run possible but do not grant autonomous destructive authority. Missing topology/recovery blocks execution, not the review or DUT verdict.
